settings.eyebrow: For the women who were told to just cope
settings.headline: The last generation of women just lived with this. You don't have to.
settings.author: Sarah, founder of Dewy
settings.byline_role: wrote this for her mum, and for herself
settings.lead: My mother spent her fifties blinking through gritty, burning eyes and never once mentioned it to a doctor. She thought it was just part of getting older — the thing you don't complain about. It wasn't. And you don't have to inherit her silence.
settings.intro_body: If your eyes feel dry, tired and gritty by the afternoon — if you've quietly started avoiding long drives at night, or reaching for drops that fade within the hour — you're part of a huge group of women nobody has really spoken to. Not because the problem is rare. Because the women who have it were raised to put up with it.
settings.s1_title: A whole generation told to just cope
settings.s1_body: Dry, irritated eyes are strongly linked to the hormonal changes of perimenopause and menopause — and they're far more common in women than men in this stage of life. Yet for decades it went unnamed and undiscussed, lumped in with all the other midlife symptoms women were quietly expected to absorb. Our mothers didn't have the language, the information, or the permission to treat it. They just blinked harder and carried on.
settings.pullquote: It was never that the problem didn't matter. It's that no one told these women it was allowed to.
settings.s2_title: You have something they never did
settings.s2_body:
Here's what's changed: we now understand the mechanism. As we age, the tiny oil glands along the eyelids slow and clog, the oily layer that stops tears evaporating thins out, and — sped along by hormonal shifts — the eyes dry faster than tears can replace. It's specific, it's understood, and it responds to a simple, well-evidenced first step your mother was never offered.

You don't have to grit your way through it the way she did. That's the whole point of Dewy.
settings.mech_intro: Dewy is a warm compress mask built around the one thing that actually helps a thinning oil layer — gentle, even warmth, held long enough to matter.
settings.mech1_body: Research indicates the eyelid needs to reach around 40°C to soften the thickened oils in the glands. Dewy holds a comfortable, even warmth across the whole lid — not a flannel that's scalding then cold in 90 seconds.
settings.mech2_body: The reason warm compresses fail people is that a hot towel is a nuisance. Dewy is a 10-minute routine you'll genuinely repeat — and consistency is the whole game.
settings.mech3_body: Washable and comfortable enough to become the nice part of your evening rather than a chore. Comfort is what turns it into a habit.
settings.mech4_body: Keep whatever your optometrist recommends. Dewy addresses the oil layer as a first-line habit — the two do different jobs.
settings.evidence_body:
We won't tell you Dewy is a cure or a replacement for anything your optometrist has given you — it isn't, and anyone who says that about a warm mask is being dishonest with you.

What's true: warm-compress and lid-warming therapy is recognised as a first-line approach for evaporative dry eye and meibomian gland dysfunction in the international TFOS DEWS II consensus, and recommended by major eye-care bodies including the American Optometric Association and American Academy of Ophthalmology. It's one of the simplest, best-evidenced first things you can do at home — often used alongside professional care.
